<a id="scope"></a>
## Scope

The manifest covers MIT's client and service library surface. D1 rows are
KDC, kadmind, database and C-ABI machinery: they are recorded as
`out-of-scope` and no API is provided for them. D2 rows are features MIT
removed or that are insecure by design: they are `rejected` with a typed
`error::RejectedFeature` and a section of
[the security policy](security-policy.md). D13 records the owner decision to
omit the legacy Windows `API:` credential cache.

Completion means the union of this manifest and
[the gokrb5 manifest](gokrb5-parity.md), not their intersection. Each row's
closing todo is the plan todo that makes it final; `P1-N` is plan 1 todo N
and `P2-N` is plan 2 todo N, listed in `docs/parity-todo-index.toml`.

<a id="rust-extension-points"></a>
## Rust extension points

MIT loads C plugin modules from `plugin_base_dir` and `module` directives. This
crate loads no code: providers are Rust values registered in an
`extensions::Registry`, and `Registry::parse_config` resolves a `module` that
names a registered provider. Any other `module` is
`Config::UnsupportedDynamicModule` in every mode.

| MIT-admin-1 | Password-change client protocol (change password / set password) | partial | unproven | WP-15 | P2-23 | Authenticated change/target-set APIs exist; expiry responder/automatic change/restart absent. | `KdcProtocol::Auto` follows changepw.c: one discovery for both protocols (`_kpasswd._udp` and `_kpasswd._tcp` are both queried and form one list; `_kerberos-adm._tcp` hosts at port 464 over both protocols only when neither set held a record, decided from the SRV answer before the targets are resolved), then TCP first over every endpoint and UDP only after the TCP pass failed; `udp_preference_limit` does not apply. A root SRV target adds no endpoint and the other records of its set are kept, as in MIT 1.22.2, which never aborts on one (dnssrv.c:332 appends a dot to every target, so the empty-host test at locate_kdc.c:380-383 cannot match, and sendto_kdc.c skips a name that resolves to nothing); with root targets only the call fails with `DnsServiceUnavailable` before any request is sent to a password server, where MIT ends in KRB5_KDC_UNREACH having sent nothing. A published set none of whose targets resolves (with `Tokio::with_dns_server`) counts as published: with no endpoint left the call fails with `KdcEndpointFailures` carrying the failure of every such set, UDP first, where MIT skips the unresolved names and ends in KRB5_KDC_UNREACH (sendto_kdc.c:753-780 and :1602-1604), and `_kerberos-adm` is asked only when the list is empty (changepw.c:68). Documented residual: the KDC path (`discover_srv_endpoints`) and the explicit `Tcp`/`Udp` discovery (its own root check in `password_dns::discover`) still discard a whole record set that mixes a root record with real records, where MIT uses the real ones. Explicit `Tcp` and `Udp` discover for their own protocol and apply the published rule to their own set (a published `_kpasswd` set of that protocol none of whose targets resolves fails with `KdcEndpointFailures` of that protocol, or with `DnsServiceUnavailable` when the set holds a root target, and `_kerberos-adm` is not asked); MIT has no explicit transport, changepw.c always runs its TCP pass and then its UDP pass over one list. Three kept divergences: (1) UDP is never tried after a TCP request that may have been delivered (the result is `KpasswdOutcomeUnknown`), where MIT kills the connection and then runs its UDP pass; (2) one datagram per endpoint with no retransmit, where MIT resends the datagram on each of up to three passes; (3) only `ConnectionRefused` or `ConnectionReset` while the single UDP reply is awaited is a plain endpoint failure and every other failure after the datagram was sent stays `KpasswdOutcomeUnknown`, where MIT treats any UDP receive error as that server failing. | - | - | - |

| MIT-trace-1 | `KRB5_TRACE` diagnostic trace logging and programmatic trace controls | implemented | fixture | WP-18 | P2-6 | - | `KRB5_TRACE` names a file (MIT `trace.c:389`, `secure_getenv`: ignored in a set-id process), read only by `trace::Options::from_env` (an opt-in constructor, in the ambient-guard inventory); the file is opened for append, mode 0600 on Unix, and each line is `[pid] seconds.micros: text` (`trace.c:411`, `:449-464`). Divergences, all on the secure side or documented: nothing is traced unless the application attaches a `trace::Guard` (`with_trace` of the exchange, the Tokio client and the acceptor; no process-wide context, no global subscriber is ever installed); principals, realms and endpoints are withheld unless `with_identities(true)`; events carry counts, numeric codes and static names only (MIT prints key hashes and message contents), so no password, key, ticket, OTP or authorization header can reach a sink; output is bounded by event, per-event byte and total-byte caps; a failing sink is counted and never changes an exchange. Events: the stepwise AS and TGS exchanges (start, request, reply, prompt, completion, failure), the Tokio client login and service-ticket calls, extension-provider events and the acceptor decision. NOT traced yet: the transport endpoint attempts (resolution, per-endpoint send), whose files todo 15 owns in this wave (register FU-TRC-P01). The `tracing` leaf forwards the same text to the application subscriber at DEBUG, failures and rejections at WARN. | `trace::Event`, `trace::Sink`, `trace::Guard`, `trace::Guard::emit`,
